variants.headline: Builder signs for a new project
variants.sub: A construction contract for {project} has been awarded to {builder}.
variants.body:
The builder {builder} has signed a contract for {project} at an agreed price of {price}. The signature establishes an undertaking to build, not a completed building. Readers assessing {target} should distinguish the award from delivery, while taking seriously the obligations the agreement is meant to create.

A builder, a project and an agreed price. Our verdict on {target}: not good enough, and the colony deserves a better standard of responsibility.

variants.headline: A price agreed, a building still to deliver
variants.sub: The company {builder} has won the building contract for {project}.
variants.body:
A price of {price} has been agreed for {project}, with {builder} winning the building contract. The project is now the subject of a signed undertaking. For {target}, the practical test concerns responsible delivery under that agreement, rather than treating a signature as proof that construction has already succeeded.

A builder, a project and an agreed price. Our verdict on {target}: not good enough, and the colony deserves a better standard of responsibility.

variants.headline: Construction contract puts obligations in writing
variants.sub: The builder {builder} has signed a contract for {project}.
variants.body:
The company {builder} has won a signed building contract for {project}. The agreed price is {price}. An assessment of {target} should begin with the responsibility attached to that undertaking, keeping the agreement to build distinct from the later task of handing over something that has actually been completed.

A builder, a project and an agreed price. Our verdict on {target}: not good enough, and the colony deserves a better standard of responsibility.
